page: Microsoft Azure EC2as_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD x86_64 processor delivering 2 dedicated vCPUs alongside 16.0 GB of system memory. Operating with an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core, the machine maintains a 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio designed to handle memory-intensive applications without requiring excessive compute allocation.

Regarding storage and acceleration, the EC2as_v6 does not include onboard local storage or dedicated hardware GPUs. Storage requirements are serviced via external Premium Storage capability, requiring attached network volumes for operating system disks and persistent application data. Network configuration includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating virtual network gateways or managed IP assignments for external connectivity.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high memory density relative to its dual-core compute profile, reducing resource overhead for workloads constrained by memory capacity rather than parallel execution threads. The primary trade-off is the reliance on remote block storage and lower compute parallelism. The instance is well aligned with small-to-medium relational database servers, in-memory caches, light data analytics, and intermediate application runtimes.
description: Microsoft Azure EC2as_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, featuring an AMD x86_64 architecture with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM. The instance provides a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, enabling efficient execution of memory-heavy tasks without over-provisioning compute resources. It operates without local disk storage, relying instead on Azure Premium Storage support for attached persistent disk volumes, and contains no hardware graphics accelerators. Network connectivity requires user-configured address routing as zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provided. By decoupling high RAM density from core count, EC2as_v6 delivers a balanced, resource-efficient option for workloads requiring elevated memory footprints without massive parallelism. It is well matched for mid-sized relational databases, caching layers, data processing pipelines, and general memory-bound backend services.
